originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches (seven named queries) and primary literature inspection did not identify the fair-reset-frequency one-crossing/stochastic-dominance theorem. Frimpong et al. 2026 provide separate densities and reset-cost formulas, but not the strict stochastic order or equal-frequency calibration. The most relevant existing own-record claim from the same paper treats Poisson exponential reset-cost singularities, not threshold versus Poisson stationary-position ordering. The single-crossing result is a meaningful additional comparison requiring a convexity/normalization proof. Residual risk from a more general published Green-potential comparison remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed general resolvent/Green-potential comparison result could imply the exact order as a corollary.
The full 2026 first-passage resetting gas text and full 2020 broad reset review were not inspected; only their abstracts were accessible.
The result applies to occupation-time costs, not the per-reset resource expenditures emphasized in the motivating paper.

value.rationale: Under a meaningful equal-reset-frequency control constraint, the result gives a distribution-wide inequality for all increasing radial occupation penalties and a structural single-crossing mechanism, uniformly across a non-power-law class of heterogeneous diffusivities. The distinction from cost incurred at a reset is physically important. It does not merely recompute the known stationary densities.
